recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed unless Patient Care reopens the AdverseEvent.code value-set scope in a new issue.
issue_request: FHIR-22735 was Published/Persuasive for STU3 AdverseEvent QA and requested changing AdverseEvent.event from the duplicate adverse-event-type value set to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/clinical-findings.
initial_application: Commit 19edc88a0ded155ed3e803b73666a87dc384f4bb changed the old source/adverseevent/adverseevent-spreadsheet.xml binding row for AdverseEvent.event from valueset-adverse-event-type to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/clinical-findings and tagged the row GF#22735.
additional_context: FHIR-22746 was a later Published/Persuasive with Modification Patient Care decision on the same element. It renamed AdverseEvent.event to AdverseEvent.code, updated the element short and definition, and narrowed/restored the event-code value set to fall plus serious-reportable-event descendants. The current build-scoped source preserves that later state: AdverseEvent.code uses adverse-event-type, while clinical-findings is now used on AdverseEvent.resultingEffect. FHIR-13312 and a 2020 Zulip thread support the same distinction between the event/code and the resulting harm/effect.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Reapplying FHIR-22735 literally to the current AdverseEvent.code element would undo the later final FHIR-22746 decision and make the current source less correct.

related_jiras.note: Later Published issue on the same element renamed AdverseEvent.event to code and intentionally restored/narrowed the adverse-event-type binding; it is already represented on the combined branch.
Earlier Applied issue said Clinical Findings was inappropriate for AdverseEvent.event and later comments identify FHIR-22746 as the effective resolution.
